audits.title: Audit of management of pregnant women with positive VDRL tests.

cycle1.result: 0.98% of pregnant women VDRL positive; only 16 of 50 seropositive women received penicillin; fetal loss in 16 (32%).

audits.other_findings: 15 of the 16 fetal losses were in women without antenatal care.
audits.citation: Mathai E, Mathai M, Prakash JA, Bergström S. Audit of management of pregnant women with positive VDRL tests. Natl Med J India. 2001;14(4):202-204. PMID: 11547524.

audits.title: Preventing congenital syphilis - a regional audit of syphilis in pregnant women seen in Genitourinary Medicine services.
audits.standard: British Association of Sexual Health and HIV guidelines on managing syphilis in pregnancy, plus locally developed standards on multidisciplinary working and communication
audits.setting: Regional audit of Genitourinary Medicine services in the north east of England

cycle1.result: 69% treated according to national guidance; all cases completed treatment. Local standards on multidisciplinary working and communication were met less well.

audits.intervention: A regional good practice guide was developed and implemented to address standards not met.
audits.other_findings: Documentation of pregnancy outcomes in GUM records and communication between specialities were particular problems.
audits.citation: Hussey J, Mitchell L, Hew Y, Foster K, Waldram A. Preventing congenital syphilis - a regional audit of syphilis in pregnant women seen in Genitourinary Medicine services. Int J STD AIDS. 2014;25(6):448-451. doi:10.1177/0956462413512802. PMID: 24285598.

audits.title: Improving the antenatal and post-partum management of women presenting to Sexual Health Services with positive syphilis serology through audit.
audits.setting: St Ann's Sexual Health Clinic, London (referrals from North Middlesex Hospital)

cycle1.result: Large proportion of referred women never attended; recorded partner notification was poor.

cycle2.result: Improved attendance, contact tracing, documentation and communication.

audits.citation: Munro CH, Henniker-Major R, Homfray V, Browne R. Improving the antenatal and post-partum management of women presenting to Sexual Health Services with positive syphilis serology through audit. Int J STD AIDS. 2017;28(9):929-931. doi:10.1177/0956462417691443. PMID: 28120643.

audits.title: Improvement of quality of care for gestational syphilis in the municipality of Rio de Janeiro.
audits.standard: Ten quality criteria and one indicator for care of pregnant women with syphilis
audits.setting: 26 primary care units, municipality of Rio de Janeiro
audits.intervention: Multifaceted: ongoing education, improved records and information systems, audit and feedback, patient education, organisational and work process changes

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 71.0% (absolute improvement 6.7%, relative 28.8%, p > 0.05); eight of ten criteria improved, four significantly.

audits.citation: Cerqueira BGT, Silva EPD, Gama ZADS. Improvement of quality of care for gestational syphilis in the municipality of Rio de Janeiro. Rev Saude Publica. 2021;55:34. doi:10.11606/s1518-8787.2021055002534. PMID: 34133619.

audits.title: Syphilis in pregnancy: a medical audit in a rural district.
audits.setting: Rural district antenatal care, Umzingwane District

cycle1.result: 1433 (66%) had an RPR result; 197 (14%) positive; 111 (67%) of 165 adequately treated.

audits.other_findings: Perinatal mortality 173/1,000 with inadequately treated RPR-positive mothers versus 21/1,000; only 42% of pregnant women estimated treated adequately.
audits.citation: Rutgers S. Syphilis in pregnancy: a medical audit in a rural district. Cent Afr J Med. 1993;39(12):248-253. PMID: 8055557.
